label: nyiso 25 steam merit
definition: KEEPER. Re-solves the nyiso-24 import-reconciliation keeper config (byte-identical flags) with ONE model-side data correction (data.fleet.MIXED_FACILITY_STEAM_HR): the Ravenswood (plant 2500, NYC) mixed CC+ST facility had its ~1.7 GW steam units inheriting the 8.8 MMBtu/MWh plant-blended heat rate (the efficient combined cycle’s efficiency leaking into the steam row), so the big NYC steam unit cleared AHEAD of idle NYC combined cycle on merit (the 2023 CC_REGULAR -4.06 / ST_GAS +3.55 TWh inversion). Recovered the steam units’ own HR (9.5) by backing the CC (~7.5) out of the 8.8 generation-weighted blend; restores the physically-correct merit order (CC ahead of steam). CC_REGULAR improves EVERY year (2023 -4.06->-3.47, 2024 -3.21->-2.61, 2025 -1.20->-0.6) and the 2023 ST_GAS over-run shrinks (+3.55->+2.76). A rule-#11 measured-data correction, forward-reproducible, not fitted to a residual. Tradeoff (kept per rule #1): C3a 2025 mean LMP +9.3% (just over +-8%) because import-constrained NYC over-relies on Ravenswood steam as marginal — a discovered symptom of the NYC import-incidence root cause (out of scope), not a reason to revert the correct HR. The RCPF scarcity tail (C3c) is unchanged: it is incidence-gated, not curve-gated (see the nyiso 25 rcpf-steep PROBE). Determination NOT-YET (the hard EIA-930/923 gas basis floor, ledgered).
